question: Should Keel get Distribution Rewards on all USDS supply of the Ethereum <> Solana bridge? Does that conflict with Pioneer Rewards?
answer:
Short answer
- Not automatically. Whether Keel (or any Prime) gets Distribution Rewards on USDS that sits in the Ethereum↔Solana bridge depends on how those bridged balances are classified/tagged and which Prime holds the relevant tag/eligibility — the Atlas defines both Distribution Rewards and separate Pioneer incentives rather than saying a Prime gets all bridged supply by default.  

Why (Atlas evidence)
- “The Distribution Reward is paid to Prime Agents that drive adoption of USDS.” [Distribution Rewards](/atlas/2177f303-a0a7-4807-b815-d17aa76a264e)  
- Net USDS balances held in a DeFi protocol receiving an Integration Boost also receive the Distribution Reward — i.e. Distribution Rewards are tied to where/because balances are supporting adoption, not an automatic grant of every bridged token supply. [Distribution Rewards (Integration Boost)](/atlas/d71a7b9c-3d0e-4383-9671-098bead326c1)  
- During the Pioneer Phase the Pioneer Prime “counts as having tagged … all USDS and sUSDS accounts and balances on the Pioneer Chain that have not been tagged by another Prime,” and untagged USDS bridged to the Pioneer Chain counts toward Pioneer Incentive payments. [Pioneer Prime Benefits](/atlas/f0d5ab5e-bf35-4a9d-a73f-d82baac6e604)  [Pioneer Incentive Pool](/atlas/c929aef7-1b81-4693-8fd8-3d75e62882af)  
- The Atlas also records that Keel is eligible for a Pioneer Incentive Pool. [Pioneer Incentive Pool — Keel eligibility](/atlas/c929aef7-1b81-4693-8fd8-3d75e62882af)  
- The SkyLink Bridge is the mechanism that moves USDS between Ethereum and Solana, but the bridge doc does not by itself assign Distribution Rewards to a Prime. [Solana SkyLink Bridge](/atlas/56593663-55e5-45d5-8682-5eede11aa14a)

Do Distribution Rewards and Pioneer Rewards conflict?
- The Atlas does not state an explicit conflict. It defines two separate mechanisms:
  - Distribution Rewards: paid to Primes that drive adoption / for net balances in boosted integrations. [Distribution Rewards](/atlas/2177f303-a0a7-4807-b815-d17aa76a264e) [d71a7b9c-3d0e-4383-9671-098bead326c1](/atlas/d71a7b9c-3d0e-4383-9671-098bead326c1)  
  - Pioneer Incentive Pool: monthly payments based on Unrewarded USDS on Solana to the Pioneer Prime’s pool; Pioneer Prime also receives special tagging rights during the Pioneer Phase. [Pioneer Incentive Pool](/atlas/c929aef7-1b81-4693-8fd8-3d75e62882af) [Pioneer Prime Benefits](/atlas/f0d5ab5e-bf35-4a9d-a73f-d82baac6e604)
- Because Pioneer Prime tagging affects which Prime is treated as the tagger for Distribution Reward calculations on the Pioneer Chain, the two mechanisms can overlap in the same balances (i.e., the same bridged Unrewarded USDS can be relevant to both programs). The Atlas does not prohibit that overlap nor prescribe a de‑duplication rule.

Practical conclusion / next step
- If you want a definitive operational rule (e.g., “Keel receives X% of Distribution Rewards on all bridged USDS” or “Pioneer payments offset Distribution Rewards”), the Atlas is silent about an explicit precedence or de‑duplication. The facilitator/governance process must interpret/decide how to handle any overlap or contested tagging. Cite: [Distribution Rewards](/atlas/2177f303-a0a7-4807-b815-d17aa76a264e), [Pioneer Prime Benefits](/atlas/f0d5ab5e-bf35-4a9d-a73f-d82baac6e604), [Pioneer Incentive Pool](/atlas/c929aef7-1b81-4693-8fd8-3d75e62882af).

If you want, I can:
- Pull the Keel instance docs (its Prime doc) and the precise “Distribution Reward Primitive” doc to show the tagging logic and any Integration-Boost definitions, or
- Draft a short governance question / motion you could file asking an explicit rule for bridge-held USDS (e.g., precedence, de‑duplication). Which would you prefer?
